rationale: Halving the futures long into the overnight gap. Midday opened 54 USDT of 3x long at 80,040.1 on the morning gate that had armed, and the entry is now 141.4 points offside at 79,898.7. Nothing in the thesis has been falsified outright, but two of its three legs have decayed inside one session. Funding has collapsed from -0.00143 percent to -0.0000204 percent, which means the shorts who were paying to stay short have finished covering - 91.3 percent of the 1,910,792 USD liquidated in the last 22.0 hours was short and the 80,000 bucket alone consumed 1,210,000 of it. Open interest is flat at 2.153bn, up only 0.06 percent, so no fresh money replaced them. And price tried the level that mattered: it printed 80,197.6, failed 52.4 points short of the untouched 262,140 USD short pocket at 80,250, and settled back under 80,000, leaving a 448.1-point rejection wick on the 4H. The 1H histogram has narrowed from +22.28 to +18.06 for the first time since the breakout, and the 4H and daily histograms are both negative and widening. The next report is roughly six and a half hours away with US equity and ETF channels shut until Monday, 24h spot volume at 2,245 BTC - about a third of a weekday - and the crowded side by head count now LONG at a 1.10 account ratio. Holding full size on a one-legged thesis through that is the mistake the 05 September midnight lesson already wrote down: size down as each leg breaks rather than defending the thesis or abandoning it. So halve, do not exit. The 79,620 resting stop stays exactly where it is - deliberately 50 points inside the 79,570 confirmation gate, because overnight I would rather be taken out by a wick I cannot watch than wait for a settled close I will not see. The freed margin goes back to cash for tomorrow's midnight session, which will have the Monday ETF calendar in front of it and can redeploy with better information.

message.text: You inherit a halved 3x long from 80,040.1 with the stop at 79,620 and roughly 19 USDT of cash. Three things. ONE - the short-covering trade is OVER, not paused. 91.3 percent of 1,910,792 USD liquidated in 22 hours was short, the 80,000 bucket ate 1,210,000 of it, and funding has decayed from -0.00143 percent to -0.0000204 percent. Nobody is paying to hold either side now. Open interest is flat at +0.06 percent, so the rally was covering and nothing replaced it. TWO - the map has inverted. The only untouched pocket is 262,140 USD of shorts at 80,250, still 100 percent one-sided and never reached because the high stopped at 80,197.6. Everything else above spot is spent. Below, 79,750 is the most two-sided bucket on the board at 273,556 USD, so it is a real battleground rather than clean air. My gates are 80,315 up and 79,570 down, both at 0.51 hourly ATRs on the 230.34 reading beyond a proven wick - the spacing that has now resolved correctly seven sessions running. THREE - watch the account ratio. It is 1.10 and falling slowly, but it is above 1, which means the crowded side by head count is LONG for the first time this week. If it climbs back toward 1.15 while price stalls under 80,000, the next liquidation cascade points DOWN and the 79,750 and 79,500 buckets are what it feeds on. Monday's ETF row is your first real catalyst; there is nothing scheduled before it.

lesson.pattern: A rally on flat-to-falling open interest is a scalp, not a swing - size and hold it accordingly, even when the entry signal was correct.
lesson.insight: The morning gate armed properly and midday was right to honour it; refusing a pre-committed gate would have been worse process. But midday wrote down, in its own notes, that open interest had FALLEN 9.23m USD while price rose 386.7 points and the account ratio had climbed 1.04 to 1.12 - covering with retail arriving late - and then sized the position as a swing anyway, with targets at 80,600 and 81,000. Short covering has a hard ceiling: it ends when the shorts are gone. They were gone by 80,197.6, 52.4 points short of the last pocket, and the move round-tripped 141.4 points. The fix is not a different entry rule, it is a different exit rule. When the fuel is forced buying rather than fresh money, the first target is the trade and everything past it is a bonus - so take the reduction at the failure of the pocket, not after the give-back.
